## ⚠️ Read this first

**This is the same channel as Video 01, and this video is a condensed version of
that course's Chapter 3 ("Option Pricing", 24:24–59:26).** Same presenter, same
three-factor pricing framework, same analogies delivered in nearly the same words
— the car-insurance-monthly-payment comparison, the smoker-vs-healthy-person life
insurance comparison, even the aside about the audience being tired of the
insurance analogy.

It is also **the oldest item in the corpus (April 2015)**, which explains why
Video 01's screen captures look dated: Video 01 is largely this era's material
assembled into a long-form course and re-uploaded in 2025.

**Consequences for the method:**

1. This does **not** count as a third independent source. The corpus currently
   holds **two** viewpoints, not three: Sky View Trading (videos 01 + 03) and
   Chart Fanatics/Usman Ashraf (video 02).
2. If cross-video agreement is what promotes a rule to "golden," counting this
   as independent confirmation of Video 01 would manufacture false consensus for
   the premium-selling thesis. It is tracked as a duplicate in `golden-rules.md`
   and carries no additional weight.
3. Its 5.2M views make it likely to appear near the top of any "top ten options
   videos" ranking — worth knowing that view-count ranking will tend to surface
   several clips from the same few channels.

---

## The one genuinely new contribution

**Time decay is non-linear.** The video states explicitly that the decay curve is
exponential rather than straight — theta bleed is slow early in the contract's
life and accelerates sharply as expiration approaches.

This is the mechanism underneath Video 02's independently-derived sizing rule
(cut position size Thursday/Friday because premium swings get violent near
expiry) and underneath Video 01's 30–60 DTE entry window. Two channels with
opposite strategies both organize their timing around the same curve. That makes
the curve itself one of the more solidly supported facts in the corpus.

---

## Everything else (all restated from Video 01)

- Three pricing inputs: time to expiration, underlying price, volatility.
- Options as insurance; longer coverage costs more.
- Strike price definition; ITM/OTM for calls and puts.
- All OTM options expire worthless; OTM options carry value before expiry only
  because the stock can still move.
- Further OTM = cheaper = less likely to pay.
- 1 contract = 100 shares, ×100 multiplier.
- You are not obligated to hold to expiration; you can close any time.
- At expiration, value = intrinsic only.
- Higher volatility = more risk to the holder = more expensive options.
- **"Volatility is much more predictable than stock prices"** — the same
  load-bearing claim as Video 01, again asserted with no evidence, again used to
  funnel viewers to the next videos in their sequence.

## Flags

- **Eleven years old.** Nothing here is wrong, but it predates the entire 0DTE
  era that Video 02 spends time on.
- **Funnel content.** It ends by pointing to the rest of their video sequence,
  same as Video 01's deferral to a paid "part two."
- **No new rules.** Nothing from this video enters the candidate list that Video
  01 didn't already contribute.

**Recommendation:** count the Sky View position once. Consider replacing this
slot with a genuinely different source — a quant/skeptic treatment, or a market
maker's perspective — so slot 3 of 10 does real work.
